meta.title: EU AI Act – Risk Tier Self-Assessment
meta.purpose: Help a provider or deployer of an algorithm or AI application determine which risk category of the EU AI Act their system falls into: out of scope, prohibited, high-risk (Annex I or Annex III), limited-risk (transparency), or minimal-risk. A separate overlay determines general-purpose AI (GPAI) model obligations.
meta.disclaimer: This tool provides non-binding, indicative guidance only. It is based on the AI Act and the Commission's draft classification guidelines (stakeholder-consultation drafts, not yet final). It is not legal advice. The final classification is the responsibility of the provider, supervised by the competent market surveillance authority. Only the Court of Justice of the European Union can give an authoritative interpretation of the AI Act. In case of doubt, consult the AI Act Service Desk, your competent authority, or qualified legal counsel.
sources: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), Articles 3, 5, 6, 7, 50, 51, 53, 55; Annexes I, III
Commission Guidelines on the definition of an artificial intelligence system, C(2025) 5053
Draft Commission guidelines on the classification of high-risk AI systems under Article 6 (general principles; Annex I; Annex III), stakeholder-consultation drafts 2026

meta.uncertaintyPolicy: Where a question is judgement-heavy, an 'I am not sure' answer is available. It always routes to the more conservative (higher-risk) branch and records a point for expert review, which is listed on the result screen.

resultModel.description: The assessment does not produce a single leaf. It produces a compiled PROFILE with up to three independent dimensions, because a system can carry more than one status at once (e.g. a high-risk system that is also subject to transparency duties, built on a GPAI model). The implementer must accumulate flags across the flow and render all applicable result cards.

dimensions.primaryTier: One of: out_of_scope | prohibited | high_risk_annex_i | high_risk_annex_iii | not_high_risk_filtered | minimal_risk. Determined by the SPINE module.
dimensions.transparency: Boolean + list of triggered Article 50 obligations. Determined by the TRANSPARENCY module. Cumulative with any tier except out_of_scope and prohibited.
dimensions.gpai: One of: none | gpai_model | gpai_model_systemic. Determined by the GPAI module. Independent of the system tier.

shortCircuits: If primaryTier = out_of_scope, stop. Do not run transparency or GPAI modules.
If primaryTier = prohibited, stop the tier spine. The system may not be placed on the market or used. Still worth noting GPAI status if relevant, but the transparency overlay is moot.

S0_ai_system.text: Does your system qualify as an 'AI system' under the AI Act?
S0_ai_system.explainer: Article 3(1) defines an AI system as a machine-based system that (a) is designed to operate with varying levels of autonomy, (b) may show adaptiveness after deployment, and (c) for explicit or implicit objectives, INFERS from the input it receives how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments. The key element is 'inference': the system derives outputs from data using techniques such as machine learning or knowledge/logic-based approaches, rather than executing only rules defined solely by natural persons.

likelyYes: Uses machine learning (supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement, deep learning)
Uses knowledge- or logic-based inference, expert systems, or search/optimisation that infers solutions
Generates content, predictions, recommendations or decisions from data with some autonomy
likelyNo: Systems for improving mathematical optimisation only, or that merely speed up classical methods
Basic data processing following rules defined solely by natural persons (e.g. a spreadsheet with fixed formulas, a static database query)
Systems based on classical heuristics with no learning/inference
Simple prediction using a single basic statistical rule

S0_ai_system.articleRef: Art. 3(1); Guidelines on the definition of an AI system (C(2025) 5053)

options.label: Yes – it meets the Article 3(1) definition
No – it only executes rules defined solely by natural persons
I'm not sure whether it 'infers'
options.reviewNote: Whether the system 'infers' outputs within the meaning of Art. 3(1) was not established. The assessment continued on the assumption that it is an AI system. Verify against the Commission Guidelines on the definition of an AI system (C(2025) 5053).

S1_prohibited.text: Does the system's intended purpose or use match any PROHIBITED practice under Article 5?
S1_prohibited.explainer: Article 5 bans certain AI practices outright (unacceptable risk). If any of the practices below applies, the system is prohibited regardless of anything else. Review each listed practice.

options.label: Yes – at least one prohibited practice applies
No – none of these apply

S2_annex_i_product.text: Is the AI system itself a product, OR a safety component of a product, covered by one of the Union harmonisation laws listed in Annex I?
S2_annex_i_product.explainer: Article 6(1) – first cumulative condition. Annex I lists EU product-safety legislation (e.g. machinery, toys, lifts, medical devices, in-vitro diagnostics, radio equipment, pressure equipment, PPE, cableways, gas appliances, and the automotive, aviation, rail and marine sectors). A 'safety component' (Art. 3(14)) is a component whose failure/malfunction endangers health and safety, OR that fulfils a safety function. Comfort/efficiency/optimisation functions are generally NOT safety functions, but a system can still be a safety component if its failure would endanger health or safety.

likelyYes: The AI is (or is embedded in) a regulated product like a medical device, machine, vehicle, lift, toy, radio equipment
The AI performs a safety function (e.g. detects human presence and triggers a safe stop; prevents collisions)
Failure/malfunction of the AI could endanger persons or property (e.g. lane assistance, lift door control)
likelyNo: The AI only optimises comfort, efficiency, performance or convenience and its failure would cause only inconvenience/cost (e.g. a smart thermostat learning routines, music recommendation in a connected toy, yield forecasting)
The product is not covered by any Annex I legislation at all

options.label: Yes – covered by Annex I legislation (as product or safety component)
No
I'm not sure (e.g. unclear whether it is a safety component)
options.reviewNote: It was not established whether the system is a product or a safety component under Annex I legislation (Art. 3(14) test). The assessment continued on the assumption that it is. Have the applicable product legislation and the safety-component test reviewed.

S3_annex_i_tpca.text: Is that product (or the AI system itself, if it is the product) required to undergo a THIRD-PARTY conformity assessment under the relevant Annex I legislation?
S3_annex_i_tpca.explainer: Article 6(1) – second cumulative condition. Both conditions must be met. Third-party conformity assessment means a notified body must be involved (conformity assessment modules other than internal-control-only module A). If the product only requires self-assessment (internal control), it is NOT high-risk under Article 6(1).

likelyYes: The applicable legislation requires involvement of a notified body (e.g. certain medical devices, many machinery categories of higher risk)
likelyNo: The product can be self-certified via internal control (module A) only

options.label: Yes – third-party conformity assessment is required
No – only self-assessment / internal control
I'm not sure which conformity-assessment route applies
options.reviewNote: The applicable conformity-assessment route under the Annex I legislation was not established. The assessment assumed a third-party assessment is required (the higher-risk reading). Check the conformity-assessment modules in the relevant product legislation.

S4_annex_iii_area.text: Does the intended purpose of the system fall within any of the specific use cases listed under the eight Annex III areas?
S4_annex_iii_area.explainer: Article 6(2). Annex III lists eight areas, but ONLY the specific use cases listed under each area count. Select every use case that matches the system's intended purpose. Many use cases apply only where the system evaluates NATURAL PERSONS (not only legal persons/companies), and some law-enforcement/migration/justice cases apply only to public authorities or those acting on their behalf, and only in so far as the use is permitted under Union or national law.

options.label: Yes – it matches at least one Annex III use case
No – it does not match any listed use case

S5_profiling.text: Does the system perform PROFILING of natural persons?
S5_profiling.explainer: Third sub-paragraph of Article 6(3): an Annex III system that performs profiling of natural persons is ALWAYS high-risk and can never use the Article 6(3) filter exemption. 'Profiling' has the GDPR meaning (Art. 4(4) GDPR / Art. 3(4) LED / Art. 3(5) EUDPR): any automated processing of personal data to evaluate personal aspects of a natural person, in particular to analyse or predict performance at work, economic situation, health, preferences, interests, reliability, behaviour, location or movements.

options.label: Yes – it profiles natural persons
No

S6_filter.text: Does the system meet at least ONE of the four Article 6(3) 'filter' conditions AND not materially influence the outcome of decision-making?
S6_filter.explainer: Article 6(3) lets a provider treat an Annex III system as NOT high-risk if it does not pose a significant risk of harm because it meets at least one of four exhaustive-but-alternative conditions (below). The overriding test is that the system must NOT materially influence the outcome of decision-making. The conditions are interpreted narrowly. NOTE: the filter does NOT apply if the system is part of a complex/agentic configuration whose combined outputs materially influence a decision in a high-risk use case, nor to Article 6(1)/Annex I systems.

subQuestion.text: Does the system materially influence the outcome of decision-making?
subQuestion.explainer: This is the overriding test in the opening words of Article 6(3). Even if one of the four conditions above is met, the exemption is unavailable when the system materially influences the outcome — including where it is part of a complex or agentic configuration whose joint outputs do.

options.label: No – it does not materially influence the outcome
Yes – it does materially influence the outcome
I'm not sure
options.reviewNote: It was not established whether the system materially influences the outcome of decision-making. The assessment treated the system as high-risk (the conservative reading). The Article 6(3) filter is interpreted narrowly; have this point reviewed before relying on the exemption.

options.label: Yes – one condition is met and the system does not materially influence the outcome
No – none of the conditions applies, or it does materially influence the outcome

T0_transparency.text: Do any Article 50 TRANSPARENCY situations apply to the system?
T0_transparency.explainer: Article 50 imposes transparency duties that are CUMULATIVE with any risk tier (they can apply to a high-risk system, a minimal-risk system, or a system that is not high-risk after the filter). Select all that apply. If at least one applies, the system carries limited-risk transparency obligations. If none applies and the system is not high-risk, it is minimal-risk.

options.label: Yes – at least one Article 50 situation applies
No

G0_gpai.text: Are you the provider of a GENERAL-PURPOSE AI MODEL (a foundation model)?
G0_gpai.explainer: This is a separate, model-level classification (independent of the system tier). Article 3(63): a GPAI model displays significant generality, is trained on a large amount of data using self-supervision at scale, and can competently perform a wide range of distinct tasks, regardless of how it is placed on the market (it can be integrated into many downstream systems). Typical examples: large language models and other large generative models. If you only USE or fine-tune a third party's model into a specific application, the GPAI-model obligations sit with the original model provider (though substantial modification can transfer them).

options.label: Yes – I provide a general-purpose AI model
No – it is a specific-purpose system, or I only deploy someone else's model

G1_systemic.text: Does the GPAI model have SYSTEMIC RISK?
G1_systemic.explainer: Article 51: a GPAI model has systemic risk if it has high-impact capabilities. This is presumed when the cumulative compute used for training is greater than 10^25 floating-point operations (FLOP), or when the Commission designates it as such. Systemic-risk models carry additional obligations under Article 55 (model evaluations, adversarial testing, systemic-risk assessment and mitigation, serious-incident reporting, cybersecurity).

options.label: Yes – >10^25 FLOP training compute or designated by the Commission
No

RESULT.text: Compile and display all applicable result cards from the accumulated flags (primaryTier + transparency + gpai).

OUT_OF_SCOPE.applicationDate: Not applicable – the AI Act does not apply.
OUT_OF_SCOPE.title: Not an AI system – outside the AI Act
OUT_OF_SCOPE.summary: Your system does not meet the Article 3(1) definition of an AI system, so the AI Act does not apply to it. Note that other EU law (e.g. GDPR, product-safety, consumer-protection law) may still apply.

PROHIBITED.applicationDate: Already in force: the prohibitions apply since 2 February 2025.
PROHIBITED.title: Prohibited – unacceptable risk
PROHIBITED.summary: The system falls under an Article 5 prohibited practice. It may not be placed on the market, put into service, or used in the EU. These prohibitions have applied since 2 February 2025.
obligations: Do not place on the market / put into service / use.
Redesign to remove the prohibited practice, or abandon.

HIGH_RISK_ANNEX_I.applicationDate: Indicative: originally 2 August 2027, postponed by the AI Omnibus to 2 August 2028. Subject to change.
HIGH_RISK_ANNEX_I.title: High-risk – Article 6(1) / Annex I (regulated product)
HIGH_RISK_ANNEX_I.summary: The system is (or is a safety component of) a product covered by Annex I harmonisation legislation AND that product must undergo third-party conformity assessment. It is high-risk under Article 6(1).
obligations: Comply with the Chapter III, Section 2 requirements for high-risk AI systems (risk management, data governance, technical documentation, record-keeping, transparency to deployers, human oversight, accuracy/robustness/cybersecurity).
Conformity assessment is carried out under the relevant Annex I legislation (integrated with the product's existing procedure).
Provider obligations under Art. 16 et seq.; deployer obligations under Art. 26.
Application date for these Article 6(1) obligations: postponed by the AI Omnibus to 2 August 2028.

HIGH_RISK_ANNEX_III.applicationDate: Indicative: originally 2 August 2026, postponed by the AI Omnibus to 2 December 2027. Subject to change.
HIGH_RISK_ANNEX_III.title: High-risk – Article 6(2) / Annex III (listed use case)
HIGH_RISK_ANNEX_III.summary: The system's intended purpose falls within a listed Annex III use case and it is not exempted (it profiles natural persons, or it does not meet any Article 6(3) filter condition / materially influences the outcome). It is high-risk under Article 6(2).
obligations: Comply with the Chapter III, Section 2 requirements for high-risk AI systems (risk management, data governance, technical documentation, logging, transparency, human oversight, accuracy/robustness/cybersecurity).
Provider obligations (Art. 16 et seq.), including registration in the EU database (Art. 49) and drawing up an EU declaration of conformity + CE marking.
Deployer obligations (Art. 26), and a fundamental-rights impact assessment where Art. 27 applies.
Application date for Article 6(2) obligations: postponed by the AI Omnibus to 2 December 2027.

NOT_HIGH_RISK_FILTERED.applicationDate: Indicative: the Article 6(4) documentation and Article 49(2) registration duties follow the Annex III timeline, postponed by the AI Omnibus to 2 December 2027. Subject to change.
NOT_HIGH_RISK_FILTERED.title: Not high-risk – Article 6(3) filter applies
NOT_HIGH_RISK_FILTERED.summary: The system's purpose is within an Annex III use case, but it qualifies for the Article 6(3) exemption because it meets a filter condition, does not perform profiling, and does not materially influence decision-making. It is therefore NOT classified as high-risk.
obligations: Document the assessment demonstrating the exemption BEFORE placing on the market / putting into service (Art. 6(4)).
Register the system in the EU database as a non-high-risk Annex III system (Art. 49(2)).
Make the assessment available to competent authorities on request.
Re-assess if the intended purpose changes: a change could make it high-risk.
Transparency obligations under Article 50 may still apply (see the transparency result).

MINIMAL_RISK.applicationDate: No mandatory obligations, so no application date.
MINIMAL_RISK.title: Minimal risk – no mandatory AI Act obligations
MINIMAL_RISK.summary: The system is not prohibited, not high-risk, and no Article 50 transparency situation applies. It falls in the minimal-risk category, which carries no mandatory obligations under the AI Act.
obligations: No mandatory AI Act obligations.
Voluntary codes of conduct are encouraged (Art. 95).
Other EU law (GDPR, consumer, product-safety) may still apply.
Re-assess if the intended purpose changes.

TRANSPARENCY.title: Transparency obligations (limited risk) – Article 50
TRANSPARENCY.summary: One or more Article 50 situations apply. These transparency duties are CUMULATIVE: they apply on top of the system's risk tier (they can accompany a high-risk, filtered, or minimal-risk classification).
obligations: Inform natural persons when they interact with an AI system, unless obvious (Art. 50(1)).
Mark AI-generated/manipulated audio, image, video or text as artificial in a machine-readable way (Art. 50(2)).
Deployers of emotion-recognition or biometric-categorisation systems must inform exposed persons (Art. 50(3)).
Deployers must disclose deep fakes and AI-generated text published to inform the public on matters of public interest (Art. 50(4)).
Application date: 2 August 2026.

GPAI_MODEL.applicationDate: Already in force since 2 August 2025. Models placed on the market before that date: comply by 2 August 2027.
GPAI_MODEL.title: General-purpose AI model (no systemic risk) – Article 53
GPAI_MODEL.summary: You provide a GPAI model without systemic risk. Model-level obligations apply in addition to any system-level classification.
obligations: Draw up and keep technical documentation of the model (Annex XI).
Provide information and documentation to downstream providers who integrate the model (Annex XII).
Put in place a policy to comply with EU copyright law.
Publish a sufficiently detailed summary of the training content (using the AI Office template).
Some documentation duties are relaxed for models released under a free and open-source licence (unless they have systemic risk).
Application date: 2 August 2025 (existing models on the market before that date: comply by 2 August 2027).

GPAI_MODEL_SYSTEMIC.applicationDate: Already in force since 2 August 2025. Models placed on the market before that date: comply by 2 August 2027.
GPAI_MODEL_SYSTEMIC.title: GPAI model with systemic risk – Articles 53 + 55
GPAI_MODEL_SYSTEMIC.summary: You provide a GPAI model with systemic risk (high-impact capabilities, presumed above 10^25 FLOP training compute, or designated by the Commission). All Article 53 obligations apply PLUS the Article 55 systemic-risk obligations.
obligations: All Article 53 obligations (documentation, downstream info, copyright policy, training-content summary).
Perform model evaluation, including adversarial testing (red-teaming).
Assess and mitigate systemic risks at Union level.
Track, document and report serious incidents to the AI Office and, as relevant, national authorities.
Ensure an adequate level of cybersecurity for the model and its physical infrastructure.
Notify the Commission when the model meets the systemic-risk threshold.
Application date: 2 August 2025 (existing models: comply by 2 August 2027).

prohibitedPractices.note: If the intended purpose matches any of these, the system is prohibited. See the Commission Guidelines on prohibited AI practices for detail.

items.label: Subliminal, purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques that materially distort behaviour and cause (or are likely to cause) significant harm.
Exploiting vulnerabilities due to age, disability, or a specific social or economic situation, to materially distort behaviour and cause significant harm.

Social scoring: evaluating/classifying persons over time based on social behaviour or personal characteristics, leading to detrimental or unfavourable treatment that is unjustified or disproportionate.

Predicting the risk of a person committing a criminal offence based solely on profiling or personality traits (with a narrow exception for supporting human assessment based on objective, verifiable facts linked to criminal activity).
Creating/expanding facial-recognition databases through untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV.
Inferring emotions in the workplace or education institutions (except for medical or safety reasons).
Biometric categorisation that infers race, political opinions, trade-union membership, religious/philosophical beliefs, sex life or sexual orientation (narrow lawful exceptions apply).
Real-time remote biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces for law-enforcement purposes (subject to narrow, authorised exceptions).

annexI_legislation.note: Non-exhaustive prompt list of the harmonisation legislation in Annex I. Section A (New Legislative Framework) and Section B (other, mostly transport). The system is in scope of Article 6(1) if it is a product, or a safety component of a product, covered by one of these.
sectionA: Lifts and safety components for lifts (Directive 2014/33/EU)
Equipment and protective systems for use in potentially explosive atmospheres – ATEX (Directive 2014/34/EU)
sectionB: Two- or three-wheel vehicles and quadricycles (Regulation (EU) 168/2013)
Motor vehicles and their trailers – general safety (Regulation (EU) 2018/858 and 2019/2144)

filterConditions.note: Exhaustive but ALTERNATIVE: meeting one is enough, but only if the system does not materially influence the outcome of decision-making and does not profile natural persons. Interpret narrowly.

items.label: Narrow procedural task
items.detail: e.g. transforming unstructured into structured data, classifying incoming documents into categories, detecting duplicates. NOT if it scores/ranks or judges data as 'useful/less useful' for a decision.

items.label: Improves the result of a previously completed human activity
items.detail: Only an additional layer to a completed human activity (e.g. improving the language/clarity of an already-drafted text). It must not replace or materially change the human's result, rights or legal/economic position.

items.label: Detects decision-making patterns or deviations, without replacing/influencing the completed human assessment absent proper human review
items.detail: e.g. flagging inconsistencies in a teacher's grading pattern for quality assurance. Ex-post comparison only; must not infer new criteria or alter the underlying reasoning.

items.label: Performs a preparatory task to an assessment relevant to an Annex III use case
items.detail: e.g. file handling, indexing, translation, that prepares but does not itself perform the relevant assessment.

overrides: ALWAYS high-risk if the system profiles natural persons (Art. 6(3) third sub-para).
Filter does NOT apply where the system is part of a complex or agentic configuration whose combined intended purpose or joint outputs materially influence a decision in a high-risk use case.
Filter does NOT apply to Article 6(1) / Annex I systems.

transparencyTriggers.note: Select all that apply. Any one triggers limited-risk transparency obligations, cumulative with the system's tier.

items.label: The system is intended to interact directly with natural persons (e.g. a chatbot / conversational agent).
items.obligation: Inform the person they are interacting with AI, unless it is obvious from the context.

items.label: The system generates synthetic audio, image, video or text content.
items.obligation: Mark outputs as artificially generated/manipulated in a machine-readable format.

items.label: The system is an emotion-recognition or biometric-categorisation system (and is not prohibited).
items.obligation: Deployers must inform the natural persons exposed to it.

items.label: The system generates or manipulates 'deep fakes', or generates/manipulates text published to inform the public on matters of public interest.
items.obligation: Deployers must disclose that the content is artificially generated or manipulated (with narrow exceptions, e.g. clearly artistic work, or human editorial review for text).

horizontalNotes: Only the specific use cases listed under each area count – not the broad area itself.
'Natural persons' limitation: several use cases apply only where a natural person is evaluated. A system that only assesses legal persons/companies is out of scope of those use cases.
'On behalf of' / public authority: several law-enforcement, migration and justice use cases apply to public authorities or private parties acting on their behalf.
'In so far as permitted under Union or national law' qualifies areas 1, 6 and 7.
Human oversight added on top does not remove high-risk classification; only the Art. 6(3) filter can.

areas.condition: In so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law.

useCases.label: Remote biometric identification systems (excluding biometric verification that merely confirms a person is who they claim to be).
Biometric categorisation according to sensitive or protected attributes/characteristics.
Emotion recognition.
Safety components in the management and operation of critical digital infrastructure, road traffic, or the supply of water, gas, heating or electricity.
Determining access, admission, or assignment of persons to education/vocational-training institutions at all levels.
Evaluating learning outcomes, including steering the learning process.
Assessing the appropriate level of education a person will receive or be able to access.
Monitoring and detecting prohibited behaviour of students during tests.

areas.area: Employment, workers' management and access to self-employment

useCases.label: Recruitment or selection of natural persons (e.g. targeted job ads, analysing/filtering applications, evaluating candidates).
Decisions on terms of work, promotion/termination, task allocation based on behaviour/traits, or monitoring and evaluating performance and behaviour.

areas.area: Access to and enjoyment of essential private and public services and benefits

useCases.label: Evaluating eligibility for essential public assistance benefits/services, and granting, reducing, revoking or reclaiming them.
Evaluating creditworthiness or establishing a credit score (excluding AI used to detect financial fraud).
Risk assessment and pricing in life and health insurance for natural persons.
Evaluating and classifying emergency calls, or dispatching / prioritising emergency first-response services (police, firefighters, medical, triage).

areas.condition: In so far as permitted under Union or national law; by or on behalf of law-enforcement authorities.

useCases.label: Assessing the risk of a natural person becoming the victim of a criminal offence.
Polygraphs and similar tools.
Evaluating the reliability of evidence during investigation/prosecution.
Assessing the risk of a person offending or re-offending (beyond Art. 5(1)(d) profiling-only prediction), or assessing personality traits/past criminal behaviour.
Profiling of natural persons in the course of detection, investigation or prosecution of criminal offences.

areas.area: Migration, asylum and border control management
areas.condition: In so far as permitted under Union or national law; by or on behalf of competent authorities.

useCases.label: Polygraphs and similar tools.
Assessing risks (security, irregular migration, health) posed by persons seeking to enter or who have entered.
Assisting in examining applications for asylum, visa or residence permits and associated complaints regarding eligibility.
Detecting, recognising or identifying natural persons in migration/asylum/border contexts (excluding verification of travel documents).

areas.area: Administration of justice and democratic processes

useCases.label: Assisting a judicial authority in researching/interpreting facts and law and applying the law, or used in alternative dispute resolution.
Influencing the outcome of an election or referendum, or the voting behaviour of natural persons (excluding tools not directly interacting with voters, e.g. campaign admin/logistics).
